heroHeadline: Day 386: US Defense Sec Hegseth at Shangri-La Dialogue Backs Trump's Ceasefire Brokering Claim — India Rejects External Mediation
heroSubtitle: May 31, 2026: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth at the IISS Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore endorsed President Trump's claim of having brokered the May 10, 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire — the most senior U.S. defense official yet to validate this narrative publicly. India formally rejects third-party mediation assertions, maintaining the ceasefire was negotiated bilaterally between DGMOs. Pakistan has actively amplified the U.S. brokerage narrative as a diplomatic asset. Hegseth's statement comes 5 days after SecState Rubio acknowledged Pakistan-sponsored terrorism at the New Delhi Quad meeting (May 26), creating a split U.S. posture: validating India's terrorism complaint while crediting the Trump-Pakistan ceasefire narrative. The ceasefire holds at Day 386 with no LOC violations since May 10, 2025. The Shangri-La Dialogue 2026 in Singapore features India-Pakistan post-Sindoor nuclear stability as a key South Asia security agenda item. The bilateral freeze continues: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT suspended and India's 'null and void' rejection of PCA's May 15 award operative. Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian airlines runs through June 23/24. India's 15 km border demolition drive across Rajasthan and Punjab border districts is in active implementation. Four confirmed back-channel contacts since May 2025 (per Al Jazeera May 23 report) remain the only bilateral communication.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
